reviews.review:
It's an okay game, but I wouldn't recommend it, especially at its price point. $20 for 14 chapters is a little steep, since the story seems a bit disjointed + too heavily written to do a sequel (almost 0 sense of closure). The main antagonist basically feels like a multi-personality disordered schitzophrenic and it throws you way off, especially since so many things could have been avoided if they spent more than 1 second to think.

Music is fine, but the art is meh (looks AI generated, and portraits do not change expressions at all + are using the battle portraits -> get cut off if you look closely) and the conversations aren't that interesting (which also applies to the characters). 

The only real saving grace for the game is the gameplay. It is pretty interesting gameplay mechanics (like elemental/debuff reactions), and all units are viable (albeit some feel harder to train but that's normal).
The issues I do have with the gameplay is that it feels very weird where almost half of the units just start off with legendary-tier infinite use weapons, and it ends up in a loop where you funnel kill set-ups into your gold-producing units, or you'll end up with no weapons for the units that don't have infinite use weapons (as most weapons have low-use before breaking).
